title: Measure, then change

blocks.promptMd: You should rewrite a loop because…

choices.md: A measurement showed it is the problem

blocks.promptMd: You should rewrite a loop because it feels slow, even with no measurement.
blocks.explainMd: Measure first. This lesson’s proof is the count from the loops you actually ran.

blocks.promptMd: > `report(n)` builds a list of `n` items, runs both searches with a counter in each loop, and returns `loops:<pairs> set:<steps>`. Count with loops — do not return a hard-coded formula string. Print `report(5)` (`loops:10 set:5`).

hintLadder.md: Two counters, two loops. Neither number should be written by hand — they must come out of the runs.
The nested pass compares each item with the ones after it, so the inner loop starts at `i + 1`.
The Set pass is one loop: add each item and increment the counter once per item.

description: Measure first. Change one thing. Measure again.
